shellRuntime.f800: As the first house of the zodiac, Aries moves before the thinking is finished. Hesitating briefly is its greatest asset — while others are still measuring, an Aries has already taken the first step. But when that speed runs ahead of checking direction, the distance back gets longer too.
shellRuntime.f801: It has the force to open a stuck situation. Aries says the first sentence where nobody else will, and restarts what has stalled. The more a moment calls for decision, the more its presence grows.
shellRuntime.f802: On days when the pace picks up, it helps to ask once: does this really have to be answered now? Mars sends drive and impulse down the same channel, so words carrying emotion are hard to take back.
shellRuntime.f803: In the morning, write your day down as just three things. The shorter an Aries list is, the higher the finish rate.
shellRuntime.f804: What is the Aries daily fortune calculated from?
shellRuntime.f805: We first compute that day's day-pillar stem and branch, the moon phase, and the flow of the solar term, then apply them to the Aries element (Fire) and ruler (Mars) to split the result into five axes: overall, love, money, health, and work. It is not written by hand each day but determined by the date, so the same day gives the same result no matter who opens it or when.
shellRuntime.f806: My birthday is near 21 March or 19 April — am I really an Aries?
shellRuntime.f807: The moment the Sun changes sign shifts by about a day from year to year. If you were born on a cusp date, the calculation needs your birth time as well. For a precise verdict, check an astrology reading that computes your birth chart directly.
shellRuntime.f808: Once Taurus settles into a place, it rarely wavers. As an earth house ruled by Venus, it has a fine eye for what is beautiful and what is comfortable, and it protects that sense for a long time. It chooses going all the way over going fast.
shellRuntime.f809: Its staying power is overwhelming. Taurus is still there after others have lost interest, and that accumulated time eventually becomes something real. Its handling of money and possessions is steady too.
shellRuntime.f810: Changing something once decided costs a lot of energy. Check now and then whether the situation has already moved while only your method stayed the same.
shellRuntime.f811: Tidy one thing you can touch with your hands — a desk, a wallet, one shelf of the fridge is enough. For Taurus, physical order leads straight to inner order.
shellRuntime.f812: Is there a reason today's money fortune matters especially for Taurus?
shellRuntime.f813: Venus, the ruler of Taurus, is read as the star of possession and value. So even at the same score, a swing in the money axis affects the whole day's condition more than it would for other houses. On days when the money score is low, simply postponing a large payment already changes how the day feels.
shellRuntime.f814: How often is the daily fortune updated?
shellRuntime.f815: When the date changes at midnight Korea time, it is recalculated with the new day pillar, and that result is reflected automatically every day. Tomorrow's fortune can be checked today, in advance.
shellRuntime.f816: Gemini stands where information passes through. As an air house ruled by Mercury, it is skilled at linking people with speech and writing, and the moment it learns one thing it tries connecting it to another. It is also the temperament that finds boredom hardest to bear.
shellRuntime.f817: It adapts to situations quickly. Gemini can open a conversation even among strangers, and has a knack for putting complicated matters into plain words.
shellRuntime.f818: When attention is hooked in several places at once, nothing gets deep. Deciding on one thing to hold onto to the end today reduces the scattering.
shellRuntime.f819: Write down whatever occurs to you, however briefly. Gemini only ever reuses what was actually recorded.
shellRuntime.f820: Why does 'speech' come up so often in the Gemini reading?
shellRuntime.f821: Mercury, the ruler of Gemini, is read as the star governing language, thought, and movement. So a day in this house is often decided in conversations, messages, and documents, and the interpretation naturally centres on that axis.
shellRuntime.f822: What is the difference between a zodiac reading and a Four Pillars reading?
shellRuntime.f823: The zodiac is based on the twelve signs the Sun travels through; Four Pillars is based on the stems and branches of the year, month, day, and hour of birth. They are different coordinate systems, so results that diverge are not a contradiction. Laying the two views over each other lets you read the same day in more dimensions.
shellRuntime.f824: Cancer is the house that takes what matters inside and guards it. As a water sign ruled by the Moon, its emotional grain is fine, and it remembers for a long time even words others let slip. Inside the hard shell is in fact the softest part.
shellRuntime.f825: It has the power to put those nearby at ease. Reading the mood first and quietly taking care of what is needed is the consideration that makes relationships last.
shellRuntime.f826: Hurt stored up inside comes out all at once later. Saying it while it can still be said small is what ultimately protects the relationship.
shellRuntime.f827: Before sleeping, bring to mind one thing you were grateful for today. In the house of the Moon, how you close a day sets the next day's condition.
shellRuntime.f828: Why is the moon phase shown alongside the Cancer reading?
shellRuntime.f829: Because the Moon rules Cancer. The Moon waxes and wanes on a cycle of about 29.5 days, and the phase shown on this page is the actual astronomical value for that date. Use it to know in advance which days are likely to bring wider emotional swings.
shellRuntime.f830: How should I read it on days when emotions are hard?
shellRuntime.f831: Rather than trying to fix the axis with the low score, we suggest using it to postpone decisions in that area by a day. A reading is not a prophecy but a reference for deciding where to spend less force that day.

shellRuntime.f1400: Jiao (角宿) is the horn of the Azure Dragon of the East, the very first of the twenty-seven mansions. Among the seven luminaries it belongs to Wood (木), so it is born with the pioneering force that pushes out first, the way a sprout shoulders the soil aside. Read through gyeokgak, it leads others from the front — and the task of this star is to gather that forwardness into one first spadeful so it does not leak away as haste.
shellRuntime.f1401: Kang (亢宿) is the straight neck of the Azure Dragon, and among the seven luminaries it falls under Metal (金). Principle and self-respect that will not soften, like wrought metal, are this star's frame. But when straightness goes too far the room turns cold, so set your principles and still leave one door in them for people to pass through.
shellRuntime.f1402: Di (氐宿) is the base of the Azure Dragon, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Earth (土). As soil holds and raises all things, this is the star of accumulation that stacks inward and firms the ground. Its grain achieves most when the roots go deep rather than when it hurries, so when impatience rises, look first at the floor you are standing on.
shellRuntime.f1403: Fang (房宿) is the belly of the Azure Dragon, assigned among the seven luminaries to the Sun (日). As the sun lights a whole gathering, this is the star of authority that holds people and leads from the front. That light draws people when it is used as care rather than rule, so lead — and call the name of whoever stands behind you first.
shellRuntime.f1404: Xin (心宿) is the heart of the Azure Dragon, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of the Moon (月). As moonlight reads what is inside the dark, this is the star of intuition that catches even what was not said. But when that sensitivity tips into suspicion you grow lonely on your own, so the stronger the hunch, the more it helps to confirm one fact before you move.
shellRuntime.f1405: Wei (尾宿) is the tail of the Azure Dragon, and among the seven luminaries it enters Fire (火). As flame cuts across a dry field, this is the star of breakthrough that drives through what is blocked. Its resilience is uncommon, but once everything has burned only exhaustion is left — so before you tear something down, decide first on one seed to plant in that spot again.
shellRuntime.f1406: Ji (箕宿) is the winnowing basket at the Azure Dragon's end, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Water (水). As water spreads wide toward low ground, this is the star of freedom that reaches out past boundaries. Its talent for widening is large but scatters easily, so however far you go, keep one harbour to return to in mind.
shellRuntime.f1407: Dou (斗宿) is the first star of the Black Tortoise of the North, assigned among the seven luminaries to Wood (木). As the Big Dipper points out a direction, this is the star of wisdom that tells others the way. When teaching runs ahead as admonition the road closes, so walking the way yourself before putting it into words carries far further.
shellRuntime.f1408: Nu (女宿) is the Weaver Maid of the Black Tortoise, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Earth (土). As one chooses thread strand by strand, this is the star of refinement that finishes by tuning the fine detail. So that an eye set on perfection does not harden into self-scrutiny, we suggest practising with 'done' as the goal rather than a hundred out of a hundred.
shellRuntime.f1409: Xu (虛宿) is the empty seat of the Black Tortoise, and among the seven luminaries it enters the Sun (日). Like the stillness after sundown, this is the star of reflection that looks inward. Emptiness becomes strength in this seat, but sink into it too long and it turns hollow — so after reflecting, always take one step back outside.
shellRuntime.f1410: Wei (危宿) is the cliff of the Black Tortoise, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of the Moon (月). As the moon waxes and wanes, this is the star that handles crisis and turning points boldly. The tighter you grip to control, the further it tips to extremes — so let go of what cannot be changed and gather your force onto the one thing that can.
shellRuntime.f1411: Shi (室宿) is the palace of the Black Tortoise, assigned among the seven luminaries to Fire (火). As one kindles a fire to raise a new house, this is the star of creation that first sets up what did not exist. Its opening force is strong but the finish is easily weak, so this time raise just one window and keep the fire burning to the end.
shellRuntime.f1412: Bi (壁宿) is the wall of the Black Tortoise, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Water (水). As water fills a crack, this is the star of mediation that joins people and settles conflict. When accommodating others costs you your own share, tuning becomes sacrifice — so check the level of your own heart before other people's balance.
shellRuntime.f1413: Kui (奎宿) is the first star of the White Tiger of the West, and among the seven luminaries it enters Wood (木). Like a scholar with brush in hand, this is the star of tradition that finishes with form and dignity. When the rule comes before the person the room turns cold, so drop one formality and lay a warm word in its place.
shellRuntime.f1414: Lou (婁宿) is the White Tiger's binding, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Metal (金). As one weaves thread, this is the star of sociability that links people and widens the circle. Wide but not deep leaves nothing to lean on, so rather than adding new ties, spend more care on the one person you will know for a long time.
shellRuntime.f1415: Wei (胃宿) is the White Tiger's storehouse, assigned among the seven luminaries to Earth (土). As one fills a granary, this is the star of accumulation that gathers resources and plans. Trying to hold everything only grows the unease, so clear out the old at regular intervals and something better takes that place.
shellRuntime.f1416: Mao (昴宿) is the White Tiger's cluster, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of the Sun (日). As many stars gather and shine, this is the star of care that holds and watches over the weaker. Weighing and measuring easily pushes people away, so when judgement runs ahead, hold first and speak later.
shellRuntime.f1417: Bi (畢宿) is the White Tiger's net, and among the seven luminaries it enters the Moon (月). As one weaves a net tight, this is the star of the artisan who completes things quietly. When diligence hardens into stubbornness it grows stifling, so leave one door open to the opinions beside you, as much as to the finish itself.
shellRuntime.f1418: Zi (觜宿) is the White Tiger's beak, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Fire (火). As a beak pecks precisely, this is the star of language where words and persuasion carry weight. Even a true remark becomes an attack when it is sharp, so grow curious before you persuade and speech turns into a bridge rather than a weapon.
shellRuntime.f1419: Shen (參宿) is the White Tiger's hunter, assigned among the seven luminaries to Water (水). As a current overturns the board, this is the star of transformation that changes what has gone stagnant. When speed outruns people, wounds are left behind — so the harder you push, the more it pays to stop briefly, look at the hearts beside you, and go on.
shellRuntime.f1420: Jing (井宿) is the well of the Vermilion Bird of the South, and among the seven luminaries it enters Wood (木). As well water runs clear, this is the star of reason that puts disorder back in order by principle. When coolness comes first the warmth dries up, so lay one layer of kind words on before you hand down a judgement.
shellRuntime.f1421: Gui (鬼宿) is the Vermilion Bird's gate, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Metal (金). As something seeps through a gap in the door, this is the star of instinct that senses the unseen and looks after people. Its moods run in large waves, so keep your own rhythm before you take others in.
shellRuntime.f1422: Liu (柳宿) is the Vermilion Bird's willow, assigned among the seven luminaries to Earth (土). As willow branches twine, this is the star of tenacity that digs to the end once it takes hold. The tighter you grip the more stifled the other feels, so loosen your hand a little and go long with a looser devotion.
shellRuntime.f1423: Xing (星宿) is the Vermilion Bird's star, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of the Sun (日). As one star shines alone among many, this is the star of contest that steps out front and leads. Fixating only on winning makes people leave, so stake the contest on one thing and let the names of those below you shine in the rest.
shellRuntime.f1424: Zhang (張宿) is the Vermilion Bird's wing, and among the seven luminaries it enters the Moon (月). As a wing spreads wide, this is the star of expression that reveals itself and draws people in. Spread it in too many places and the charm thins, so today stand on one stage alone and show yourself deeply there.
shellRuntime.f1425: Yi (翼宿) is the Vermilion Bird's other wing, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Fire (火). As one preens the feathers to finish them, this is the star of quality and courtesy. When correction comes out first the room stiffens, so mind the finish — and say out loud what the other person did well before anything else.
shellRuntime.f1426: Zhen (軫宿) is the carriage of the Vermilion Bird of the South and the last of the twenty-seven mansions. Assigned among the seven luminaries to Water (水), it is the star of closure that sets down neatly what it has carried. Trying to tidy everything perfectly easily postpones the decision, so do not weigh it — finish the one thing in your hand today, for certain.
shellRuntime.f1427: Ashwini is the first star, ruled by Ketu, with the dawn healers the Ashwini Kumaras as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to heal quickly' — a Deva (divine) temperament laid over a Vata (wind) constitution gives it a grain that begins and restores anything at speed. The growth point of this star is practising to carry what it started all the way through, so that hurry does not leave things unfinished.
shellRuntime.f1428: Bharani is ruled by Venus, but its deity is Yama, god of death and rebirth. Its shakti is 'the power to take away and purify' — the star of transformation that sends the old off and lets the new in. A Manushya (human) temperament carries the motive of Artha (achievement), giving it the grit to digest even a burden that looks too heavy to bear.
shellRuntime.f1429: Krittika is ruled by the Sun, with Agni, god of fire, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to burn and purify' — Rakshasa (fierce) concentration meets the motive of Kama (creativity), giving it a sharpness that cuts away impurity without mercy. That fire shines most when it is used to warm others, so do not forget the warmth you hold before you cut.
shellRuntime.f1430: Rohini is ruled by the Moon, with Brahma (Prajapati) the creator as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to make things grow' — Kapha's steadiness blends with the motive of Moksha (spirituality) to draw in material abundance and beauty. It is bright to the pleasures of the senses, and it needs an eye that watches the flow so they do not become attachment.
shellRuntime.f1431: Mrigashira is ruled by Mars, but its deity is Soma, the gentle moon god. Its shakti is 'the power to find fulfilment' — a Deva temperament carries a pure searching spirit, making it a deer-like star always roaming after something. Only when that curiosity meets a resting place does the heart settle.
shellRuntime.f1432: Ardra is ruled by Rahu, with Rudra, god of storms, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to change through effort' — taking a teardrop as its symbol, the grain of this star is the deep empathy that arrives after upheaval. Vata's change meets the motive of Kama, so rather than pushing on, tend to the recovery that follows the storm.
shellRuntime.f1433: Punarvasu is ruled by Jupiter, with Aditi the boundless mother as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to regain abundance' — the star of return that rises again however many times it loses. A Deva temperament carries the motive of Artha, and not losing its optimism is this star's greatest asset.
shellRuntime.f1434: Pushya is ruled by Saturn, but its deity is Brihaspati, the teacher-god of Jupiter. Its shakti is 'the power to nourish spiritual force' — it is counted the most auspicious of the twenty-seven. A Deva temperament meets the motive of Dharma (calling), and fullness comes to it from raising and caring for others.
shellRuntime.f1435: Ashlesha is ruled by Mercury, with the serpent deity Naga. Its shakti is 'the power to coil and permeate' — Rakshasa insight meets Kapha depth, making it the mysterious star that sees through the subconscious. That insight shows its true worth when it is used for healing rather than for binding.
shellRuntime.f1436: Magha is ruled by Ketu, with the ancestral Pitrs as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to carry on the root' — the star of authority and inheritance, taking a throne as its symbol. Rakshasa force carries the motive of Artha, and it earns respect in the seat where it guards and continues what was handed down.
shellRuntime.f1437: Purva Phalguni is ruled by Venus, with Bhaga, god of delight, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power of the joy of union' — a Manushya temperament carries the motive of Kama, making it the creative star that enjoys love, art and pleasure. Life brightens when it expresses that joy without fear.
shellRuntime.f1438: Uttara Phalguni is ruled by the Sun, with Aryaman, god of contracts and friendship, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to accumulate and prosper' — the star that builds lasting relationships out of trust and generosity. A Manushya temperament meets the motive of Moksha, and the more it gives, the more prosperity returns.
shellRuntime.f1439: Hasta is ruled by the Moon, with Savitr, the creative power of the Sun, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to hold what one wants in the hand' — the star of skill and realisation, taking the hand as its symbol. A Deva temperament carries the motive of Moksha, and it draws healing and reward from what it makes with its fingertips.
shellRuntime.f1440: Chitra is a star forged by Mars, with Vishwakarma, the cosmic artisan, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to shape merit' — taking a bright jewel as its symbol, it pursues beauty and technical perfection. Rakshasa concentration meets the motive of Kama, so when that keenness is aimed at one thing, a masterpiece follows.
shellRuntime.f1441: Swati is ruled by Rahu, with Vayu, god of wind, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to scatter and spread' — like a young sprout swaying in the wind, independence and flexibility are this star's grain. A Deva temperament carries the motive of Artha, and it finds its balance inside an unbound freedom.
shellRuntime.f1442: Vishakha is ruled by Jupiter, with the union of Indra and Agni as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to reap many fruits' — the star of purpose and final victory, taking a triumphal arch as its symbol. Rakshasa ambition carries the motive of Dharma, giving it uncommon concentration on a goal.
shellRuntime.f1443: Anuradha is ruled by Saturn, with Mitra, god of friendship, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to serve and devote' — taking the lotus as its symbol, it grows through sincere devotion and love. A Deva temperament meets the motive of Dharma, and it finds deep satisfaction in serving people.
shellRuntime.f1444: Jyeshtha is ruled by Mercury, with Indra, lord of the thunderbolt, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to contend and win' — the star of courage, protection and leadership, taking an amulet as its symbol. Rakshasa force carries the motive of Artha, giving it the grain that steps out and fights in order to protect.
shellRuntime.f1445: Mula is ruled by Ketu, with Nirriti, goddess of dissolution, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to tear out by the root' — taking bound roots as its symbol, it is the star of truth-seeking that digs down to the foundation. Rakshasa intensity carries the motive of Kama, and this star's wisdom is deciding what seed to plant again in the place it tore open.
shellRuntime.f1446: Purva Ashadha is ruled by Venus, with Apas, the water deity. Its shakti is 'the power to raise the spirits' — purification and an undefeated persuasiveness, taking a fan as its symbol, are this star's grain. A Manushya temperament carries the motive of Moksha, and it is skilled at lifting other people's morale.
shellRuntime.f1447: Uttara Ashadha is ruled by the Sun, with the Vishwadevas, the assembly of ten cosmic gods, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power of victory that does not collapse' — the star of merit and endurance, taking the elephant's tusk as its symbol. A Manushya temperament carries the motive of Moksha, and it holds out long enough to arrive rightly in the end.
shellRuntime.f1448: Shravana is ruled by the Moon, with Vishnu the preserver as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to join and carry on' — the star of listening and of spreading knowledge, taking the ear as its symbol. A Deva temperament carries the motive of Artha, and it earns trust and achievement by listening well and passing things on.
shellRuntime.f1449: Dhanishtha is ruled by Mars, with the Ashta Vasus, the eight gods of abundance, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to give abundance and fame' — the star of music, rhythm and wealth, taking the drum as its symbol. Rakshasa force carries the motive of Artha, and renown for leading a group, along with plenty, tends to follow.
shellRuntime.f1450: Shatabhisha is ruled by Rahu, with Varuna, god of cosmic law, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the mysterious power to heal' — the star of healing and independence, taking an empty circle ringed by a hundred stars as its symbol. Rakshasa depth carries the motive of Artha, and it finds its answers inside a mystery it digs into alone.
shellRuntime.f1451: Purva Bhadrapada is ruled by Jupiter, with Aja Ekapada, the flame of what is to come, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the fiery power to raise the spirit' — the star of spiritual awakening and transformation, taking two faces as its symbol. A Manushya temperament carries the motive of Artha, giving it uncommon heat toward an ideal.
shellRuntime.f1452: Uttara Bhadrapada is ruled by Saturn, with Ahir Budhnya, the serpent of the deep, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to send rain and steady things' — the deep wisdom of the subconscious, taking a serpent in the water as its symbol. A Manushya temperament carries the motive of Moksha, and insight ripens inside its quiet patience.
shellRuntime.f1453: Revati is ruled by Mercury, with Pushan, god of journeys, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to guard the road and complete it' — the last star, of nurture and of return, taking the fish as its symbol. A Deva temperament carries the motive of Moksha, and it closes the journey with the warmth of seeing the lost safely home.
shellRuntime.f1454: The Sukuyo master reads Jiao as the first stretch of Wood (木), the Azure Dragon's horn breaking through the sky ahead of everyone. The Jyotish master sees the same seat as Chitra, a star cut by Vishwakarma, the cosmic artisan, with the 'shakti that shapes merit'. Two masters point at one thing in different languages — the power to begin earlier and sharper than others.
shellRuntime.f1455: The grain does part, though. Sukuyo welcomes Jiao as an auspicious pioneering star, while the Vedic side sees fierce Rakshasa concentration in Chitra. Which is to say the talent for beginning is also the seed of haste. That tension is what makes you distinctive — and what tires you easily.
shellRuntime.f1456: You are the one who puts the first spade into ground nobody has opened. But aim the stretch of Wood and the keenness of Mars at several places at once and the blade dulls. Pick the single thing to begin today and raise your horn only there — gathered into one, pioneering becomes a masterpiece.
shellRuntime.f1457: The Sukuyo master reads Kang as the Azure Dragon's straight neck, a principle as unyielding as metal (金). The Jyotish master sees Swati, the independence and flexibility given by Vayu, god of wind. Two readings that look opposed in fact name one axis — a centre of your own that nobody can swing.
shellRuntime.f1458: But Sukuyo's Kang is a principle that firmly holds, while the Vedic Swati is a flexibility that lets go like wind. Holding and flowing live in one body — knowing when to stand fast and when to release is the work of your life.
shellRuntime.f1459: Your standards do not bend easily. When that metal hardness turns a relationship cold, leave one gap inside the principle for Vayu's wind to pass through. Straight but soft is the person trusted longest.
shellRuntime.f1460: The Sukuyo master reads Di as the accumulation of Earth (土), the Azure Dragon's base quietly firming its roots. The Jyotish master sees Vishakha, the star of final victory where Indra and Agni join to 'reap many fruits'. Both traditions point at the same grit — the power to stack one step at a time and arrive in the end.
shellRuntime.f1461: But Sukuyo sees Di as a 'steadiness' that stacks inward, while the Vedic side sees Vishakha as an 'ambition' aimed outward. Between the force that firms inward and the force that charges outward, your pace is decided.
shellRuntime.f1462: You may not be flashy, but you are the one who sees things through. Only, when the harvest (Vishakha) dazzles you, you can shake the roots (Di) you already laid. When impatience rises, check the floor you are standing on first.
shellRuntime.f1463: The Sukuyo master reads Fang as the authority of the Sun (日), the Azure Dragon's belly that gathers a room and leads it. The Jyotish master sees Anuradha, the star of 'serving and devoting' given by Mitra, god of friendship. The force that leads from above and the force that serves from beside meet in one seat — leadership that holds people as it leads them.
shellRuntime.f1464: But Fang's authority comes down 'from above', while Anuradha's devotion rises 'from beside'. Turn it into rule and people move away; turn it into devotion and they follow. The balance of leading and serving is what matters.
shellRuntime.f1465: You are the one people naturally put at the centre. Use that solar authority as Mitra's care rather than as an order, and nobody leaves. Lead from the front — and call the name of whoever stands behind you first.
shellRuntime.f1466: This is one of the rare seats where the Sukuyo master and the Jyotish master point at the same star, Antares. Sukuyo reads Xin as the Moon's (月) intuition, the Azure Dragon's heart; the Vedic side sees Jyeshtha as the 'contending and winning' insight given by Indra, lord of the thunderbolt. The two traditions meet at the same red star in the sky — and speak of an eye that sees first what others cannot.
shellRuntime.f1467: But Xin is a quiet 'intuition', while Jyeshtha is the Rakshasa 'courage' that fights in order to protect. Whether the power to see through becomes insight or suspicion — that fork decides your relationships.
shellRuntime.f1468: You are the one who notices even what was not said. When that moonlit sensitivity tips into assuming, it makes you lonely. The stronger the hunch, the more it helps to take Indra's courage and confirm one fact before you move.
shellRuntime.f1469: The Sukuyo master reads Wei as the breakthrough of Fire (火), the Azure Dragon's tail cutting across a blocked field. The Jyotish master sees Mula, the power to 'tear out by the root' given by Nirriti, goddess of dissolution. Two masters point at the same intensity — the force that will not rest until it sees the end.
shellRuntime.f1470: But Wei is a 'breakthrough' that drives forward, while Mula is 'dissolution and rebirth' that breaks the old and plants again. Advancing and tearing down live in one body — what to break and what to leave is what matters.
shellRuntime.f1471: You are the one who comes alive precisely at a dead end. Only, if you burn everything with Fire and tear everything out with Nirriti and have nothing left to raise, all that remains is exhaustion. Before you pull it down, decide first on one seed to plant in that spot.
shellRuntime.f1472: The Sukuyo master reads Ji as the expansion of Water (水), the Azure Dragon's winnowing basket spreading wide. The Jyotish master sees Purva Ashadha, the undefeated persuasion that 'raises the spirits', given by Apas the water deity. Both are stars of water — they speak of the force that reaches far past boundaries and leads people.
shellRuntime.f1473: But Ji is a search that 'scatters' freely, while Purva Ashadha is a carrying-through that 'must persuade'. Scattering and carrying-through sit together — and freedom without direction blows away easily.
shellRuntime.f1474: You are the one who feels stifled when tied to one place. The talent for widening is large, but without one harbour to hold what you started, nothing is left. Go far — and settle on one place to come back to.
shellRuntime.f1475: The Sukuyo master reads Dou as the wisdom of Wood (木), the Big Dipper pointing out a direction. The Jyotish master sees Uttara Ashadha, the 'victory that does not collapse' given by the Vishwadevas, the ten cosmic gods. Both traditions say the same thing — the power to hold out long and arrive rightly in the end.

shellRuntime.f1480: You are the one who cannot let even a small misalignment pass. Do not let that weaver's delicacy turn into a whip aimed at yourself. Rather than heading for a hundred out of a hundred, listen first with Vishnu's ear and practise leaving one thing today at 'done'.
shellRuntime.f1481: The Sukuyo master reads Xu as the stillness after the Sun (日) has set, the Black Tortoise's empty gate that looks inward. shellRuntime.f1483: You are the one who draws strength from time alone. But sink too long and it turns hollow, so fill the emptied place with one rhythm of the Ashta Vasus. After reflecting, always take one step back outside.
shellRuntime.f1484: The Sukuyo master reads Wei (危) as the turning of the Moon (月), the Black Tortoise's nerve standing at the cliff. shellRuntime.f1486: You are the one who grows clearer exactly where others fall apart. But trying to hold everything in hand turns that force against you. With Varuna's wisdom, let go of what cannot be changed and concentrate on the one thing that can.
shellRuntime.f1487: The Sukuyo master reads Shi as the creation of Fire (火), the Black Tortoise's palace raising a new house. shellRuntime.f1492: You are the one who lays a bridge across a rift. But in trying to fit everyone, there are times you lose yourself. With Ahir Budhnya's depth, check the level of your own heart today before you steady anyone else's balance.
shellRuntime.f1493: The Sukuyo master reads Kui as the tradition of Wood (木), the White Tiger's dignity with brush in hand. shellRuntime.f1495: You are the one who closes anything with proper form. But when Kui's rule comes before the person, the room turns cold. As you finish, drop one formality and lay one of Pushan's warm words in its place.
shellRuntime.f1496: The Sukuyo master reads Lou as the sociability of Metal (金), the White Tiger's binding that weaves thread. shellRuntime.f1498: You are the one who opens people up quickly even among strangers. But wide and not deep leaves nothing to lean on. Rather than adding new ties, spend more of your heart today on the one person you will know for a long time.
shellRuntime.f1499: The Sukuyo master reads Wei (胃) as the accumulation of Earth (土), the White Tiger's storehouse filling its granary. shellRuntime.f1500: But Wei is resource management that 'stacks' steadily, while Bharani is a fierce 'transformation' that sends the old off and lets the new in. Stacking and emptying sit together — hold on only, and unease grows; let it flow, and it becomes a reorganisation.
shellRuntime.f1501: You are the one who keeps resources and plans without a gap. But trying to hold everything only grows Yama's unease. Clear out the old at regular intervals — something better comes into the space you emptied.

shellRuntime.f1504: You are the one who cannot simply walk past someone weaker. Agni's sharp eye lives in you too, so when judgement runs ahead, hold first and speak later. Before you burn, be the one who warms.

shellRuntime.f1513: You are the one who cannot bear stagnation and changes it. But when speed outruns people, wounds are left. The harder you push the reform, the more it pays — like Rudra's tears — to stop briefly, look at the hearts beside you, and go on.
shellRuntime.f1514: The Sukuyo master reads Jing as the reason of Wood (木), the Vermilion Bird's order clear as well water. shellRuntime.f2100: Even people who share the same animal symbol shine quite differently, depending on the season of their chart, the tilt of the five elements and where they sit in the twelve life stages. One prepares quietly and grows strong at the decisive moment; another moves fast from the start but has to learn staying power separately. The codex draws that difference out gently, so you neither exaggerate nor hide what you are good at.
shellRuntime.f2101: Saju Palja transcribes the year, month, day and hour of your birth into two characters each, builds an eight-character chart, and reads where the five elements crowd together and where they run empty. The eight characters themselves never change for a lifetime, but ten-year major cycles and one-year annual cycles pass over them, so even for the same person the theme in the foreground shifts with the period. This is not a way of sorting good charts from bad ones. Seeing which force is currently excessive and what is missing — and setting a direction to make up for it — is what actually proves useful. The calculation that builds the chart and the reading of the five-element and ten-god placements are automated, and AI interpretation is used to turn the result into sentences, so the same chart is read differently to suit the period and the question.
shellRuntime.f2102: In relationships it also shows whose presence puts you on the defensive, and what kind of setting opens your heart. In work and money it shows the way strength gathers naturally, rather than when you force it. The destiny animal does not stop at a cute image — it reads as a symbol pointing to the rhythm you need to recover in your life now, and the attitude you should grow next.
shellRuntime.f2103: Even within one element, the grain of the sixty-jiazi differs. Jiazi is not Yichou, Bingwu is not Dingwei — the same fire and the same wood still surface in different ways. Compressing that difference into the name and the sentence of a seal is the real work of this reading. It is cultural content built on a traditional system of symbols, and cannot be used as grounds for medical, legal or investment decisions.
shellRuntime.f2104: Your animal is not a playful name that guesses today's mood — it is closer to a mark carrying the direction of a vitality built up over a long time. Read where you turn cautious and where you turn bold, beside whom you soften and in front of what work your strength returns, and the rhythm of your life starts coming back a little clearer and a little easier.
shellRuntime.f2105: When you read the result, it is better not to stop at the animal's name but to look at how that symbol comes alive in the currents of love, work and money. A reaction that felt like a familiar weakness may, read properly, be wisdom your body learned in order to survive a long time; and a strength that never showed itself easily will clearly bloom once it meets the right season.
shellRuntime.f2106: This codex is arranged so you can look at your core disposition, your instinct for work and money, your habits in love and relationships, and the mission that grows you, all at once. The animal symbol looks light, but the reading opens deep along the flow of your chart, and the closing sentences point at a direction you can hold in your hand today rather than pronouncing on your life.
shellRuntime.f2107: The flow of the twelve life stages in your natal chart quietly shows at what speed a person's force unfolds and in what manner they bind themselves to the world. The Destiny Animal Codex carries that flow over into animal symbols, gently lighting the survival instinct that has long lived in you, the direction of your growth, and the movements that repeat in your relationships.
shellRuntime.f2108: Having your saju read easily turns into hearing what is good and what is bad. Saju Guardian turns that around and first raises the force in your chart that works to protect you. Enter your birth date and hour, and it fixes three coordinates — the day pillar, the month branch and the hour branch — lays the generating and controlling cycles of the five elements over them, and opens a single guardian seal.
shellRuntime.f2109: A myeongni reading gains its force in the moment you act on it, not in the moment you read it. So the result ends not with interpretation but with today's fortune-opening ritual. It leaves you one small action with clear edges — a colour to keep near, a standard to tidy by, a sentence to say out loud — and lays a seven-day guardian mission on top of it.
shellRuntime.f2110: The grain of the twelve life stages — birth, bathing, capping, prosperity, emperor, decline, illness, death, tomb, severance, conception, nurture — is less a personality table than a map for reading the rhythm of a life. When you move out in front, when you step back, and in which relationships your strength recovers rise calmly to the surface over the seasonal feel of your chart.
shellRuntime.f2111: Saju compatibility sets two charts side by side and reads how the eight characters act on each other. There are three layers to it. First, what relation the two day stems stand in. Next, whether the five elements of the two charts supply what the other lacks, or push harder on the side that is already overflowing. Last, where the ten gods interlock — in particular, which of the other person's characters meets the spouse palace on the day branch. Seeing what is caught in each of these three layers is more useful to a real relationship than a single score that compresses everything into one number.
shellRuntime.f2112: Sometimes learning to rest comes before learning to be strong, and sometimes the moment arrives to bring out into the open a sense you have quietly kept. The animal symbols of the twelve life stages tell you those turning points kindly, and light the direction in which you can trust yourself more naturally.
shellRuntime.f2113: This animal reading looks at both the force that moves first inside your chart and the force that holds out longest behind it. What matters more than the personality you show on the outside is which situations open your heart wide, and under what pressure you instinctively lower your body.
shellRuntime.f2114: The places where the force of a chart comes strongly alive differ from person to person. One chart softens its expression in wide-open space; another shares what it truly means indoors, in the quiet. Even in a familiar neighbourhood there is an alley where the grain of connection opens, and even in an unfamiliar travel spot there is a direction in which the heart closes easily. This consultation reads that difference through the senses of the five elements and the seasons, and tells anyone preparing for a meeting which stage will feel more natural.
shellRuntime.f2115: Month branch — the background in which the seal gains its force in reality. Just as the Tiger month that opens the door of spring differs from the Ox month that stores winter's end, the same seal is put to different use depending on which season's ground it stands on.
shellRuntime.f2116: The month branch is the earthly branch of the month you were born in. Even with the same day pillar, the way a seal gains force changes with the month whose ground it stands on, so the reading takes the twelve backgrounds and reads each in its own sentences.
shellRuntime.f2117: The place spoken of here is not simply a place name but an environment where your force catches its breath comfortably and meshes naturally with the force of others. A walking path where the force of wood comes alive, a concert hall where the force of fire spreads warmly, a café where the steadiness of earth settles, an exhibition space where the clarity of metal shows, a travel spot where the flow of water deepens — the grain of connection becomes distinct inside the character of a place.
shellRuntime.f2118: Connection never arrives wearing the same face. For one person the heart opens on a road near water, for another in an old alley and a quiet bookshop, and for another in the evening light of an unfamiliar city. Reading the place of connection through saju follows the seasons and the flow of the five elements held in your birth date, and reads finely which spaces and moods make it easy for the door of a relationship to open for you.
shellRuntime.f2119: The place of connection does not mean only far-off travel. A corner you often pass, the seat in a café where you loosen up, a shelf you want to linger at, a walking path where the air clears after rain — scenes that match your force open in places very close by too. What matters is whether that space keeps you from overstating yourself, and lets you meet people wearing your most natural expression.
shellRuntime.f2120: Love is not decided by a place alone, but an environment where the heart can settle changes the first breath of a relationship. Look together at the grain of a city that suits you, a good hour to arrange a meeting, a route that tires you less, an atmosphere in which conversation deepens easily — and you no longer have to force a connection. In the spot where your force shines comfortably, a meeting opens more quietly and more clearly.
shellRuntime.f2121: The feeling of loving your favourite is one thing, but the way that feeling gets spent differs from person to person. For some the emotion moves first; for others the strength goes into staying beside them for a long time. Oshi Destiny takes both birth dates, the names and the current mood, splits that difference across four axes and scores them, and mixes the four axes at different weights to produce the overall score.
shellRuntime.f2122: Hour branch — the secondary rhythm by which your guardian force wakes within a day. The waterway of the Rat hour and the high noon of the Horse hour point to different times, so entering your birth hour opens the timing of your actions as well.
shellRuntime.f2123: After hearing compatibility as a score, two things usually remain: one number, and the feeling of not knowing what you are supposed to do about it. LOVE CODE walks you through situations instead of explaining the result in words. It stands a character with the temperament drawn from the other person's birth date in front of you, and each choice you make in a date scene actually moves the relationship's numbers.
shellRuntime.f2124: The four axes are not indicators that rank one above another. If emotional resonance comes out high and the long-term current low, that is not bad compatibility — it is closer to meaning that your heart is moving with the temperature of the moment right now. Seeing how the shapes of the four axes are out of step with each other is more useful than the scores themselves.
shellRuntime.f2125: The energy type is made by attaching the five-element label drawn from your birth season to the birth date reduced to a single digit. The connection keywords mix the force and focus drawn from both names with the favourite-mood and relationship-mood you entered, and pick up to five without repeats. Put in the same values and you get the same result, whenever you press it.
shellRuntime.f2126: Earth — the force of centre and storage. When you gather scattered work and build a structure, the floor of your fortune firms up, and your force runs clear where you separate your share from other people's.
shellRuntime.f2127: The result is not that person's actual character — it is the temperament drawn from the birth date you entered, moved into a character. Facing the same partner, a different choice from you produces a different ending, so what this simulation actually shows is less the other person than the habits of choice that repeat in you inside a relationship.
shellRuntime.f2128: Metal — the force of discernment and completion. Build up the power to draw a line through a blurred situation, but you also need to shape the order so that your standard does not sound like a verdict.
shellRuntime.f2129: The report also lights the spaces where a meeting opens easily, the hours in which you grow closer, the mood that softens a first conversation, and the overdone staging you would do better to avoid. Rather than pulling love in by force, it is a way of finding the spot where your force shines most naturally, and making the empty room in which a connection can stay.
shellRuntime.f2130: The five numbers are not independent of one another. A choice that raises tension can pull chemistry up with it, and if you only ever make the safe choice, stability holds but chemistry loses its place. The structure reveals not which choice is correct, but which side you are the sort of person to pick by default.
shellRuntime.f2131: Water — the force of insight and flow. It lets you hear the essence even inside anxiety, but once your instinct arrives you have to open a channel with a small experiment, or the action falls behind.
shellRuntime.f2132: Wood — the growing force that stretches upward. It works toward cutting a path through a blocked current, and trimming your priorities the way you prune branches becomes the core of your protection.

shellRuntime.f2339: Reunion tarot is not a sentence that settles your waiting; it is a reading that checks the distance you need right now for contact and recovery. Time after a breakup does not run at the same speed for two people. Often one is still standing in front of the last conversation while the other has already moved into the next season, and reaching out without knowing that gap replays the same scene once more. So this reading does not begin by asking whether you will meet again. It sets what remains in your heart, the grain visible in the other person, and the real reason contact stopped, each in its own position. The Starlit Night Sea reunion fortune is made of five positions, and the last one deals not with whether you reunite but with what it would take to break the same pattern once you are close again.
shellRuntime.f2340: When your heart is worn out, the hardest thing is not making the feeling go away but naming what is draining you right now. Healing Rising Tarot divides that work into four positions. It lays one card at a time in the order of cause, acknowledgement, learning and action, and closes the reading at the last position with a single action small enough to try within today.
shellRuntime.f2341: The four positions are not split into good cards and bad cards. The first two explain your present state and the last two point at a direction, so reading only the front feels heavy and reading only the back leaves out the grounds. Rather than drawing again and again in a short span, it is steadier to come back after a day has passed or the situation has changed.
shellRuntime.f2342: Other's Heart Tarot is not a divination that guesses someone's inner mind; it is a reading that separates the signals you are currently reading in the other person from the words actually exchanged, and shows the gap between them. When a relationship feels unstable we attach layers of meaning to one short reply or one postponed plan, and much of that interpretation comes from our own state, not from them. So this reading sets the feeling on the surface, the motive underneath it, and the guesswork you added, each in its own position. What to check and what to stop asking is decided here.
shellRuntime.f2343: This reading is content for entertainment and self-reflection; it does not stand in for psychological counselling or diagnosis. For decisions about health, law, investment, treatment or safety, please turn to a professional body first. The basic reading is free to use without signing up.
shellRuntime.f2344: What confuses us most about someone's feelings is usually the actions rather than the words. When they clearly said something warm yet the replies keep slowing, or they act cold yet never quite leave, we want to pin their real intention down in one sentence. But relationships do not move that simply. The feeling can remain while the defences run larger; the liking can be there while responsibility grows heavy enough to make them step back.
shellRuntime.f2345: The more unsettled our feelings, the more we press for an answer out of a wish to be reassured. But what usually saves a relationship is not a grand statement — it is smaller, more concrete choices: timing, the length of a sentence, the way you ask, the interval you leave before waiting again. This reading sorts out exactly that. shellRuntime.f3173: Zi Wei Dou Shu builds twelve palaces from the hour of birth and places the Zi Wei star and its companions across them, reading how much weight each area of life carries. Where the Four Pillars look at the balance of energy, Zi Wei Dou Shu looks at where that energy has gathered. If you are looking for a place to have a Zi Wei reading done, begin by drawing your own chart and reading outward from the Life Palace to the Wealth, Career and Spouse palaces. Reading the Wealth Palace on its own shows when the money side of a Zi Wei chart starts to move, and laying the Four Transformations and the major fortune periods over it shows when that area turns especially noisy. Read alongside a Four Pillars reading, the two fill in each other's blanks.
shellRuntime.f3174: Zi Wei Dou Shu can look like a bare list of stars, but read properly it makes clear where a life catches its breath and where it gives off light. What matters more than waiting for a good season is preparing a vessel that fits it, and even a heavy season is never entirely a closed road. The in-depth reading follows the conversation between stars and palaces, and shows calmly what scene today's choice will grow into later.
shellRuntime.f3175: The depth of Zi Wei Dou Shu does not end with knowing many star names; it opens where you can read how different palaces speak to one another. A strong star in one palace can lighten the load in another, and the movement of the Four Transformations can call a long-postponed decision out into the open. This reading weaves those signals together calmly so that you can see the direction of your work, relationships, money and state of mind more clearly.
shellRuntime.f3176: If the Life Palace lights up the centre of a life, the Body Palace shows the attitude that settles into you as time passes. The Parents and Siblings palaces speak of the grain of relationships that run from your roots, and the Travel Palace points to the scenery in which your fortune widens when you step outside. The Health Palace has you watch the small signals your body and mind send, and the Friends Palace quietly tells you who to keep close and which ties need distance.
shellRuntime.f3177: Zi Wei Dou Shu is a system in which twelve palaces, centred on the Life Palace, divide up the areas of a life. Rather than lumping a whole destiny together, it works by pointing to the palace where your current question sits and reading the stars and transformations resting there. Where the Four Pillars speak of temperament in the single language of the five elements, Zi Wei Dou Shu divides the areas of life across the map of the palaces.
shellRuntime.f3178: An in-depth reading does not stop at the placement of the major stars; it reads the movement of the Four Transformations, the time axis of the major fortune periods, and the answering echo between one palace and another. In some seasons choices open quickly; in others the ties and skills you have already built quietly come to fruit. The flow across a chart does not lock destiny into a fixed conclusion — it points to which attitudes and decisions sit more naturally in your present reality.
shellRuntime.f3179: The most important thing when reading a chart is not simply sorting stars into good and bad. You have to look together at where a star sits, the angles at which they light one another, and the order in which their force switches on within the flow of time. Some stars feel like a burden in youth and turn into responsibility and authority with the years; others open brilliantly at first but demand restraint and balance if they are to last.
shellRuntime.f3180: So an in-depth Zi Wei reading does not pin your present frustration on a single cause; it works it loose carefully within the relationships among several palaces. When tension in the Spouse Palace, pressure in the Career Palace, the flow of the Wealth Palace and fatigue in the Fortune Palace tangle together, life asks for deep adjustment rather than a simple choice. The chart works like a quiet star map showing the order in which to make those adjustments.
shellRuntime.f3181: The movement of the major fortune periods in particular shows when the scenes of a life deepen and when they lighten. Reading the meaning of a season already past and looking ahead at the force of one approaching lets you tell apart what must be seized quickly from what can quietly be waited out. The stars do not command; they light a direction, and within that light choices grow calmer and firmer.
shellRuntime.f3182: A Zi Wei chart spreads a life across twelve palaces and looks in three dimensions at the flow of temperament and relationships, work, wealth, health, movement, marriage and family. The Life and Body palaces set the basic direction from which you view your life, and the stars placed in each palace tell you where you shine strongly and where careful adjustment is needed.
shellRuntime.f3183: The twelve palaces work like twelve different rooms of a life. The Career Palace lights the grain of work and social standing, the Wealth Palace reveals how money comes in and stays, and the Spouse and Fortune palaces show the relationships in which the heart rests and the satisfaction felt within. Read together, a finer map of a life emerges than any fragmentary score could give.
shellRuntime.f3184: An expert Zi Wei reading builds a twelve-palace chart from your birth date and hour, then reads the star placements in the Life and Body palaces, the movement of the Four Transformations, and the grain of the major and annual fortunes you are passing through. shellRuntime.f3627: Today's fortune is a reading of the grain made when the day's pillar (one of the sixty stem-branch combinations) meets your own chart. The day pillar itself is the same for everyone, but which themes come to the fore depends on the relation it forms with your day master. So on the same day, relationships surface for one person and work for another. It is more genuinely useful as a reference for deciding where to spend your strength today and what to put off by a day, rather than as a fixed schedule. Unlike readings that look only at your animal sign or star sign, a birth-date fortune raises all four pillars, so even within the same animal sign the area that stands out today differs from person to person.
shellRuntime.f3628: The names of those relations are the ten gods. If today's heavenly stem is the same element as your day master it becomes Companion or Rob Wealth; the element you produce gives Eating God or Hurting Officer; the element you govern gives Indirect or Direct Wealth; the element that governs you gives Indirect or Direct Officer; and the element that produces you gives Indirect or Direct Resource. Even the same god reads in reverse depending on whether your chart is strong or weak. A chart with energy to spare benefits from a god that drains it; a chart short of energy benefits from one that fills it. That is why the same day is highly auspicious for one person and a day for caution for another.
shellRuntime.f3629: To this is added tāra bala, which counts how many places today's lunar mansion sits from your own natal mansion. Where it falls among the nine positions — Janma, Sampat, Vipat, Kshema, Pratyari, Sadhaka, Vadha, Mitra and Atimitra — indicates the day's fortune. On timing, we also show Rāhu kālam (the stretch of the day to avoid) and Abhijit muhūrta (the short auspicious window around noon). These two windows assume a standard six o'clock sunrise and six o'clock sunset, so they differ from actual times with the season.
shellRuntime.f3630: If the heavenly stem is the surface of a day, the earthly branch is its floor. When today's branch clashes with your day branch (the branch of the day you were born), travel and changes of appointment become frequent; when they bind through six or three combinations, conversation and collaboration go smoothly. To this we add the auspicious and inauspicious stars — Heavenly Noble, Literary Star, Travelling Horse, Peach Blossom, Canopy, Yang Blade, Void — showing only those that catch on today's branch. Finally we score the twelve two-hour periods of the day, from Rat to Pig, by the same criteria, separating the hours where your strength lands from those to hold back a beat.
shellRuntime.f3631: The five are vāra, tithi, nakṣatra, yoga and karaṇa. Vāra is the weekday and its ruling planet. Tithi is the lunar day that turns over each time the moon moves 12 degrees away from the sun, split into the brightening fortnight (shukla) and the darkening fortnight (krishna). Nakṣatra is the one of twenty-seven lunar mansions the moon now occupies, each with its own ruler, deity, symbol and particular power. Yoga is the sum of the solar and lunar longitudes divided into twenty-seven, and karaṇa is one of the sixty halves of a tithi.
shellRuntime.f3632: There are six angular relations. The same seat is Destiny; nine places apart is Karmic Womb; one place is Glory-Kin; two is Friend-Decline; three is Peace-Ruin; four is Fulfil-Peril. Even within the same relation the meaning flips depending on which side you stand on. The Glory seat gives and makes the other shine, the Kin seat leans and receives, and the Decline seat gives out until it is worn down. So this screen shows not only the name of the relation but which role today puts you in.
shellRuntime.f3633: Each of the twenty-seven mansions has its own direction and element, its guardian among the four spirits (Azure Dragon, Black Tortoise, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird), and its own archetype. Horn is pioneering, Neck is principle, Root is inner substance, Chariot is completion — each different in character. Reading today's mansion for both its strength and its shadow makes it far clearer what to spend time on and what to hold back from, even on days of the same grade.
shellRuntime.f3634: The day pillar is the one stem-branch pair of the sixty assigned to a given day. One heavenly stem pairs with one earthly branch, and the same characters come round every sixty days. The day pillar itself is the same for everyone, but the meaning of the day depends on the relation it forms with the day master of your chart — the heavenly stem of the day you were born. That relation is exactly what this screen calculates.
shellRuntime.f3635: The three tabs above read the same day in different ways. The Four Pillars calculate with the sixty-year cycle, Sukuyo astrology with the twenty-seven mansions the moon occupies, and Vedic astrology with the actual positions of the heavenly bodies. Where the three results diverge, take it as a day on which judgement is divided. Below is an explanation of what each item means.
shellRuntime.f3636: Where the today's fortune above is a personal reading calculated from your birth date and time, below are free fortunes recalculated and published each day for the twelve star signs and the twelve animal signs. shellRuntime.f3637: Vedic astrology takes the moon, not the sun, as the measure of a day. The Vedic items on this screen actually compute the sidereal longitudes of the sun and moon at noon today using the Swiss Ephemeris, and raise the five limbs of the Pañcāṅga from them. Pañcāṅga means literally "five (pañca) limbs (aṅga)".
shellRuntime.f3638: Sukuyo astrology divides the twenty-seven days the moon takes to circle the sky into twenty-seven seats. The seat fixed by the lunar date of your birth is your natal mansion, and the seat the moon occupies today is today's mansion. The relation between the two is set by the forward distance between them, and this is called the angular relation.

shellRuntime.f3674: Physiognomy is not a technique for judging people by their faces; it is a system that sets out, by traditional rules, what impression each of the five features and each area of the face creates. This page introduces those rules while advising against using the result as a verdict on character. What is actually useful is not the features you were born with but the things you can adjust — expression and tone of voice. Because the same face gives a different impression depending on the expressions it wears most often, physiognomy is most practical when used as a mirror for reviewing how you present yourself, not as a yardstick for judging others.
